newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker on last minute flurry.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker on last minute flurry.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended lower at $1.3881 (US$0.7204) on Monday from Friday's close of C$.3835 (US$0.7225) after a flurry of last minute trading, dealers said.
* They said the currency weakened in the dying minutes of interbank trading on concerns over possible interest rate moves in the United States and Canada.
Nasato said there were a lot of last minute discussions about interest rates and whether the Bank of Canada would try to resist pressure to follow a U.S. move up.
"The talk I've heard is because of interest rate spreads," Nasato said. "They believe the Bank of Canada will hold (if the Fed raises interest rates)."
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee will hold its next meeting July 1-2. Any interest rate moves would likely come after the meeting ended.
But dealers added that they thought the Canadian dollar would not weaken past C$1.3895 (US$0.7196) overnight.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar fell to 81.37 yen from Friday's 82.65 and dropped to 1.2298 marks from 1.2461 marks.
